[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 240
- Description: Oscar Nibs QR batch: decode escalation, movement guard, and custody reconciliation
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/659
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/663
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/665
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/666
  
  Details:
  Closes out the Oscar Nibs (2024OSCAR_20250826_NIBS) QR-code handling thread: decoding the bag photos, diagnosing two ledger defects that surfaced from it, correcting the QR registry, and shipping three tools plus two SOP rules so the failure modes cannot recur.
  
  WORK PERFORMED
  
  1. QR decoding pipeline (PR #663)
  Gemini vision returned 404 on every call — root cause was retired model names plus sending the key as a query param instead of a header. Fixed model selection and moved to the x-goog-api-key header. Then shipped qr_decode_escalate: pyzbar over a crop/upscale ladder -> Gemini multi-model consensus (>=2 must agree) -> OCR of the printed companion label, returning confidence and needs_human. A single vision read is never treated as truth, because vision models confabulate digits on dense QR matrices. 23 tests.
  
  2. SOP: OCR failure fallback (PR #663)
  docs/QR_CODE_OCR_FALLBACK_SOP.md documenting the escalation ladder and the never-guess-a-digit rule.
  
  3. SOP: photo-driven movements must move individual QR codes (PR #665)
  New rule: when photos yielding QR codes drive an [INVENTORY MOVEMENT], the QR Code field must list every decoded code and Quantity must equal the code count. Booking SKU + quantity alone is redefined as a balance adjustment, not a movement of identifiable bags. Five-point pre-flight plus a narrow exception for genuinely non-serialized bulk SKUs, explicitly not available merely because decoding was inconvenient.
  
  4. Enforcement guard (PR #666)
  validate_inventory_movement implements the above as a callable pre-flight check, with 16 tests, one per decision path. Design constraint set by the governor: the guard keys off whether QR codes were SUCCESSFULLY EXTRACTED, not whether an attachment exists. An early version keyed off attachment presence and would have blocked legitimate work — a governor attaching a photo of himself with the buyer for the record contains no codes at all. Absence of evidence is not evidence of error. Blocks: extracted codes omitted, partially listed, disputed/needs_human, or quantity disagreement. Permits: no codes extracted, no attachment, unreadable photo, non-serialized bulk.
  
  5. verify_dao_submission_landed (PR #659)
  Edgar returns HTTP 200 on accept but the sheet append runs through an async Apps Script webhook that can lag minutes. This tool polls until the marker appears and distinguishes timeout (still queued — do NOT resubmit) from genuine failure. Written after an operational mistake in this thread: twice reporting "nothing landed" when the append was merely queued, which invites duplicate ledger rows. 17 tests.
  
  LEDGER DIAGNOSIS
  
  6. Rows 6126/6127 confirmed quantity-only
  Field-by-field read of the submission bodies: 6126 (-19) and 6127 (+19) carry no QR Code field and no attachment — bare balance adjustments on the origin SKU. The re-booking legs 6128/6129 carry all 19 individual QR codes. Consequence: for the reversal legs there is no per-bag traceability; which specific bags left Kirsten is recoverable only by inference from 6128/6129. This is the concrete evidence now cited in the #665 SOP rule.
  
  7. Root-caused why the QR registry still showed Kirsten as manager
  Initial hypothesis (the three hard-to-decode photos never got optically confirmed, so their manager was never updated) was WRONG, and is recorded here as wrong. Two facts disprove it:
   - report_inventory_movement.py contains no QR-registry write path at all (grep for QR tab / update_qr / qr_code_sheets -> zero matches). It writes the offchain transactions row and nothing else.
   - All 19 codes remained MINTED under Kirsten Ritschel — not just 3.
  The registry is genuinely live but is written from other paths: NIBS_22 shows SOLD under Matheus Reis, and the tab holds 1241 MINTED / 620 SOLD / 90 SAMPLE across 2,012 codes. So sales update it; inventory movements never do. Custody in offchain asset location was already correct throughout (Gary Teh 19 / Kirsten Ritschel 110 = 129 landed), meaning the movement succeeded and nothing was broken. The gap is observability: QR status is not custody after any movement.
  
  8. QR registry corrected (governor-directed)
  Set the Manager Name column (col U) for all 19 NIBS codes from Kirsten Ritschel to Gary Teh. Dry-ran first to confirm row numbers and column, then a single 19-cell batch_update (one API call, no partial-write window), then a fresh read-back: 19/19 verified, no collateral rows touched. status and Sold Date deliberately left MINTED, since custody transfer is not a sale.
  
  TESTING
  Full suite green at merge time for #666: 2625 passed, 2 skipped, 4 xfailed, 3 xpassed, 0 failed. ruff clean on all newly added files (all 21 findings in the first draft of the guard fixed, including an ISC004 trailing-comma). compileall and ruff format clean.
  
  NOTED, NOT ACTIONED
  - No QR-registry write path in report_inventory_movement.py. Future movements carrying QR codes likewise will not update the Manager column. Parked as a known gap; changing it means touching a 2,012-row shared registry and deciding a history backfill.
  - The guard is a pre-flight check, not a hard refusal inside dao_client. Wiring it into report_inventory_movement.py is a separate change with a larger blast radius.
  - config/nginx/sophia.conf and data/active_tracks.json remain locally modified on the autopilot box and uninspected.
  - Autopilot box sits on feat/qr-decode-escalate rather than main; a redeploy from there would run stale code.
  
  No production deploy. No ledger events submitted. No funds or TDG moved.
- Contributor(s): Gary Teh
- TDG Issued: 400.00
- Attached Filename: N/A
- Destination Contribution File Location: N/A
--------
